prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Generate 5 ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question, each with a short title and a description of one or two sentences. Sample the ideas from the full distribution of possible responses, and give each idea its estimated probability of being generated (a number between 0 and 1).

ideas.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN of AP-1 occupancy after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Profile chromatin accessibility and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding at timepoints after a transient stimulus and long after its withdrawal. Persistently open AP-1 motif-containing enhancers would indicate a retained memory state.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation (primed vs. naive) transcriptional response assays
ideas.description: Expose cells to a first stimulus, rest them, then re-stimulate and measure target gene induction by RNA-seq or qPCR. Faster or stronger induction in primed cells compared with naive ones, and its loss on AP-1 inhibition, would test whether AP-1 is required for memory.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 perturbation (dominant-negative, degron, CRISPRi) during priming vs. recall
ideas.description: Disrupt AP-1 with a dominant-negative such as A-FOS, an auxin degron on JUN/FOS, or CRISPRi, either only during the priming phase or only during recall. This separates the role of AP-1 in establishing memory from its role in maintaining it.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage tracing/live reporters
ideas.description: Use single-cell RNA+ATAC, or live AP-1 activity reporters tracked through cell divisions, to see whether the memory state is inherited by daughter cells. Test for heterogeneity and bistability in AP-1 activity and accessibility.

ideas.title: Pioneer-factor and chromatin-state analysis at memory loci
ideas.description: Combine histone modification profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me1), BAF/SWI-SNF occupancy, and DNA methylation with AP-1 motif mutation by CRISPR or base editing. This tests whether AP-1 sites are causally needed to keep enhancers primed, and whether memory persists once AP-1 itself is lost.
